# EF loading, tracking and query shape

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `ef-loading-performance` · **EF Core & LINQ** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S02-Q032](#S02-Q032)

<p>What causes an N+1 query pattern in EF Core, and how would you prove that it occurs in one endpoint?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Choose and verify an EF Core query shape that returns the required data without unexamined database work.</p>

<ul>
<li>Explain related-data loading and entity-tracking boundaries.</li>
<li>Locate database versus application evaluation using command evidence.</li>
<li>Diagnose N+1 from access traces and query counts.</li>
<li>Compare alternatives with equivalent results and representative measurements.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [LINQ execution and result cardinality](ef-query-execution.md)

<p>Tracking and evaluation questions clarify what the context and database are responsible for. Eager-loading configuration applies those boundaries to related data. N+1 diagnosis then tests what actually ran; strategy comparisons choose a response to that evidence. Projection and generated SQL bring the group to production validation: neither a familiar API nor fewer LINQ lines proves a suitable query.</p>

### S02-Q027 · Mechanism

<p>For one EF Core workload, how would you compare lazy, eager and explicit loading of related data?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q027](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q027)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q027](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q027)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare Lazy Loading, Eager Loading, and Explicit Loading.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare when related data is requested and what the application knows beforehand. Relate the choice to the required result rather than assuming one loading style always wins.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a loading strategy using access patterns and query evidence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name EF Core version, provider, lazy-loading configuration and relationship cardinality; check official support and inspect emitted commands.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace the same data access under each candidate strategy.</li>
<li>Compare round trips, returned data and failure boundaries with a measurement plan.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Ranking strategies without workload context or assuming lazy loading is enabled.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How does unpredictable navigation access affect your choice?</li>
<li>What would you measure when two collections are needed?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q029 · Mechanism

<p>What does AsNoTracking() change in an EF Core query, and when would that choice fit the unit of work?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q029](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q029)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q029](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q029)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What does `AsNoTracking()` do and when should it be used?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the relationship between queried entities and the context that manages changes. Judge the option by later use of the results, not merely by calling it a performance switch.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose tracking behavior from entity use and persistence requirements.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State EF Core version, provider and query shape; consult official tracking and identity-resolution documentation before asserting detailed behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace reading and later editing the same result under the chosen mode.</li>
<li>Specify correctness checks and a measurement before claiming an improvement.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming no-tracking means no database locks or that every later edit is automatically persisted.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What changes if the response requires repeated references to the same entity?</li>
<li>How would you make a later update explicit in this design?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q030 · Mechanism

<p>How would you distinguish server-side and client-side evaluation in an EF Core query?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q030](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q030)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q030](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q030)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain server-side versus client-side evaluation.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain which operations run in the database and which run in application memory. Use one expression to expose the boundary and its consequences for data transfer and correctness.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Locate an evaluation boundary using provider and command evidence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify EF Core version, database provider and expression position; consult official evaluation rules because support and failure behavior are version-sensitive.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace the expression to database commands and local processing.</li>
<li>Test an unsupported expression and explain the effect of moving the boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming any C# expression translates or describing historical provider behavior as a current default.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would an earlier materialization change the amount of data transferred?</li>
<li>What evidence shows where the filter actually ran?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q028 · Application

<p>How would you configure eager loading for the relationships required by a specific EF Core query?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q028](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q028)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q028](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q028)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you configure Eager Loading?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Identify the object graph the caller needs and show how the query requests it. An object graph is the set of related objects needed for that response, not every relationship in the model.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Translate required related data into an inspectable query configuration.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name EF Core version, provider and relationship shape; check official Include/ThenInclude support and any selected query-splitting behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Map required relationships to the configuration and verify the returned graph.</li>
<li>Inspect commands and data volume rather than assuming one efficient SQL statement.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Including every navigation property without considering result size or actual callers.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you verify that a nested relationship is loaded?</li>
<li>When would a projection meet this response contract more directly?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q032"></a>

### S02-Q032 · Failure cases

<p>What causes an N+1 query pattern in EF Core, and how would you prove that it occurs in one endpoint?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q032](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q032)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q032](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q032)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What causes N+1 queries and how do you detect them?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>N+1 describes an initial query followed by additional queries associated with individual results. Connect the pattern to the access path and evidence, not only to a loading-strategy label.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Diagnose repeated database calls and verify a targeted correction.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name EF Core version, provider and loading configuration; inspect command evidence with realistic result counts before asserting a cause.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace which access triggers repeated commands and compare query counts as results grow.</li>
<li>Verify a changed loading or projection strategy preserves results and improves the measured symptom.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Declaring N+1 from slow response alone or assuming every loading problem has the same fix.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you distinguish N+1 from one expensive database query?</li>
<li>What other cost could increase after reducing the round trips?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q031"></a>

### S02-Q031 · Production decision

<p>How can projection and generated SQL affect an EF Core query, and how would you verify a proposed improvement?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q031](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q031)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q031](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q031)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do projection and generated SQL affect performance?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Projection selects the shape of the returned data. Connect that shape to the response contract and actual database work instead of assuming fewer lines of LINQ imply less work.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Validate a query-shape change with equivalent results and workload evidence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State EF Core version, provider, representative data and response fields; use official tooling documentation for command inspection.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Compare result equivalence, selected data and emitted commands before and after.</li>
<li>Propose measurements that separate database work, transfer and application allocation.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Promising a speedup from shorter LINQ without inspecting SQL or checking correctness.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What if the projection introduces an extra related-data query?</li>
<li>How would you choose representative data for the comparison?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Agent-added production exercise: an endpoint returns a page of departments and their employee summaries; latency rises as the page grows. Capture its commands, returned data and application work. Determine whether repeated related-data calls or one expensive query explains the symptom, propose a loading/projection/tracking change, and test equivalent results and boundary cases. Name EF Core/provider versions, verify documented behavior, and compare representative before/after measurements without inventing a speedup.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains the loading options, tracking purpose and meaning of N+1.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Locates the evaluation and access boundaries; diagnoses using command evidence; defends a query-shape change and verifies correctness plus workload costs.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Naming Include or AsNoTracking is not evidence of an improvement. Need emitted commands, equivalent-result checks and actual measurements, or a clearly stated plan to obtain them.</p>
